title: Implement OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN or remove dead macro + false comment (post-reboot nonce-reuse hazard)
description: oscore.h:132 OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN(1024) referenced NOWHERE; oscore_protect.c:224 comment cites nonexistent persist_ssn bump. Consequence: NVM-fail after output built + reboot before successful persist reloads stale SSN -> sender collides with already-transmitted seq (nonce reuse, RFC 8613 7.2). PRE-EXISTING at HEAD. Preferred: implement real bump in oscore_ctx_persist_ssn (persist then advance RAM+NVM sender_seq by margin so post-reboot seq strictly greater than any pre-crash transmission); update comments + host harness test proving post-reload seq > pre-crash max. Alternative if bump breaks persistence budget: document limitation prominently + remove false comment.
close_reason: Implemented the PREFERRED path: real OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN in oscore_ctx_persist_ssn (oscore_ctx.c). On every successful NVM write it now stores sender_seq + OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN and - only after success - advances the in-RAM sender_seq to the same durable value, monotonically and only after re-locking and re-validating slot identity (index/active/peer_eui64); on NVM failure after the 3 retries the in-RAM SSN is left exactly as before (protect-path reservation rollback still works). Deliberate deviation from the bead's literal 'cap at OSCORE_SSN_MAX', honoring the bead's own stronger invariant: the durable cap is the exhaustion sentinel OSCORE_SSN_MAX + 1 because a reloaded OSCORE_SSN_MAX could re-transmit the terminal five-byte PIV after a crash that used it (nonce reuse); a reloaded sentinel makes protect_request refuse with SEQ_EXHAUSTED (key rotation required), which is the RFC 8613 7.2/Appendix D.4-correct outcome. No-callback case stays a full no-op (no skip, RAM untouched) so all legacy NULL-callback behaviors are preserved byte-for-byte. Skipped range is never used as a nonce; skipping semantics documented at the macro, persist_ssn, protect_request, NVM-callback and NVM-failed-enum docs in oscore.h, at the protect.c persist call site, and in the protect_response SECURITY block. Persistence format audited: the write_cb/read_cb contract is a full uint64 with no range checks on reload (create_with_eui64 assigns raw, protect refuses >MAX), so margin/sentinel values round-trip without format change; verified by harness. Verified: (1) host harness (temp dir oscmargin-verify) compiling the REAL oscore TUs + vendored monocypher + tinycrypt AES-CCM with stub zephyr headers, ASan+UBSan clean, output: A PIV=100 RAM/store=1125; B reboot reload 1125 > 100, next PIV=1125; B2 exact skip jumps +1025, reload 3075 > max 2050; C NVM-fail leaves RAM 100, exact retry PIV=100 then 1125; D no-callback legacy +1; E terminal PIV MAX-2 caps store/RAM at sentinel 2^40, reloaded sentinel refused (-8 SEQ_EXHAUSTED); F store->reload identity. (2) clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra on all 7 oscore TUs at PT_MAX 256/2048 x MAX_CONTEXTS 8/32, clean. (3) ztest suite updated for the new contract (test_nvm_read_failure_fallback_to_zero, test_nvm_protect_request_nvm_failure, test_protect_request_rolls_back_before_publish now assert next-unused + margin in RAM and NVM) and two new tests added (test_persist_ssn_safety_margin_prevents_reboot_reuse, test_persist_ssn_margin_caps_at_exhaustion_sentinel) - these encode the NEW contract; they run via twister/native_sim in CI and could not be executed on this Mac (known unreliable native_sim per AGENTS.md); the host harness above runs the identical scenarios against the same TUs and passes.
